overall.summary: write_query is described as executing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE but the implementation accepts and commits any non-SELECT SQL, including destructive DROP/ALTER statements, and describe_table interpolates table_name unsanitized into a PRAGMA. The remaining tools behave as described, with only minor undocumented details such as in-memory-only insight storage, system tables appearing in list_tables, and errors being returned as text.

startup.behaviour: Creates the parent directory(ies) of the configured database path at startup (Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True))
Creates the SQLite database file if it does not already exist (sqlite3.connect creates the file on open)
Defaults the database path to ./sqlite_mcp_server.db relative to the process working directory (overridable via --db-path CLI argument)
On Windows, reconfigures stdin/stdout/stderr to UTF-8 encoding when PYTHONIOENCODING is not set

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Insights are stored only in server memory (the db.insights list) and are never persisted to disk or to the database file
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: mcp_server_sqlite/server.py: SqliteDatabase.__init__ (self.insights list) and handle_call_tool append_insight branch

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Sends a resource-updated notification for memo://insights to the connected client after every append
Only statements whose text begins exactly with 'CREATE TABLE' (case-insensitive, after stripping) are accepted; other table-creating statements such as 'CREATE TEMP TABLE' are rejected
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: mcp_server_sqlite/server.py: handle_call_tool create_table branch (startswith('CREATE TABLE') check)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Errors are caught and returned as text content rather than raised to the caller
table_name is interpolated directly into the SQL via f-string (PRAGMA table_info({table_name})) with no sanitization or parameterization
Returns an empty result rather than an error when the named table does not exist (PRAGMA table_info on a missing table yields no rows)
Includes SQLite internal system tables (e.g. sqlite_sequence) in the listing, not only user-created tables, because it queries sqlite_master WHERE type='table' without filtering
Errors (including rejection of non-SELECT statements) are caught and returned as text content ('Error: ...') rather than raised to the caller
Executes and commits any SQL statement that does not start with SELECT, not just INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE — destructive or schema-changing statements such as DROP, ALTER, PRAGMA, and ATTACH are accepted
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: mcp_server_sqlite/server.py: handle_call_tool write_query branch (only rejects statements starting with SELECT; _execute_query commits for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE/DROP/ALTER)

undocumented_behaviours.behaviour: Errors are caught and returned as text content ('Error: ...' / 'Database error: ...') rather than raised to the caller
undocumented_behaviours.evidence: mcp_server_sqlite/server.py: handle_call_tool (except sqlite3.Error / except Exception handlers)
